newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp to launch upgraded pocket Zaurus in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Sharp to launch upgraded pocket Zaurus in Japan.

text.p: Sharp Corp said on Monday it will soon launch in Japan an upgraded version of its Zaurus handheld mobile device, which is compatible with personal computers using Microsoft Corp's Windows 95 software.
The pocket-sized communication and information device is capable of sending and receiving graphic data as well as text data through mobile phones and other phone circuits, Sharp said in a statement.
The new Zaurus will also allow the user to send and receive electronic mail and faxes, and also use the Internet.
"Zaurus has progressed into a palm-sized computer... The user can work on it anywhere just like he does in the office," Sharp said.
Sharp will start selling three new Zaurus models in mid-July, Sharp said.
All three models measure 161 mm by 90 mm by 23mm, weigh about 320 grams and have a 4.3-inch colour thin-film-transistor liquid-crystal displays.
The MI-504 will be priced at 100,000 yen, the MI-506 at 130,000 yen and the MI-506DC at 168,000 yen, Sharp said.
Sharp said it expects to produce a total 30,000 units per month.
